title: Security Trading Policy & Insider Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: The Board; directors and company secretary of any subsidiary; any person entitled to receive equity performance rights and/or options under an equity incentive scheme of the Company; any Executives; and the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associated Parties
tiers.description: Immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust of a Restricted Person.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company

windows.start_anchor: 5 business days before the announcement of a dividend or any other capital management initiative that might have a material impact on the share price
windows.end_anchor: the announcement of the dividend or other capital management initiative

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board has absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their associated parties trading in the Company's securities at any time, and the Company may from time to time designate further prohibited periods. Confidentiality of an embargo is not addressed.

rules.detail: No standalone derivatives rule exists. An OTC put or call over Company shares is a 'financial product' that operates to limit the economic risk of holding the shares, so it is caught by the absolute hedging ban, which applies without qualification by tier, vesting state or clearance route.
rules.evidence: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute, unqualified ban on hedging arrangements over Company securities (shares, options and rights) for all Restricted Persons and associated parties; no clearance mechanism, no distinction by vesting state.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).

rules.detail: The policy does not separately address monetisation structures beyond the hedging ban.
No provision addresses short selling of Company securities.
No provision addresses lending Company securities to a third party.
A CFD referencing Company shares is a financial product that limits the economic risk of holding the shares and so falls within the absolute hedging ban.
rules.evidence: Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.

rules.detail: Including Company securities in a margin loan portfolio, transferring securities into an existing margin loan account, or selling to satisfy a margin call, each require the Company's prior consent, which may be made subject to conditions (e.g. the circumstances in which shares may be sold to satisfy a call).
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.

rules.detail: Granting a general charge, lien or pledge outside a 'margin lending arrangement' is not separately addressed.
The policy only names 'margin loan'/'margin lending arrangement'; it has no broader catch-all for other secured financing in respect of Company securities.
No minimum holding period or anti-flipping provision.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (who confers with the Chairperson)
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's securities, by themselves or their associated parties, prior to such intended dealings.

clearance.approver: Chairperson (or another Director if the Chairperson is involved)
clearance.evidence: clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so. ... The Chairperson must determine, and specify in the written clearance, the maximum duration of the clearance.

exceptions.evidence: undertakings or elections to take up entitlements under a rights issue or other offer (including an offer of securities in lieu of a cash dividend)
the sale of sufficient entitlements to allow take up of the balance of the entitlements under a rights issue
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or pursuant to a scheme of arrangement implemented in accordance with section 411 of the Corporations Act

transfer of securities arising out of the operation of an employee scheme into a savings scheme investing only in securities of the Company following: (i) the exercise of an option under a savings related securities option scheme; or (ii) release of securities from a profit sharing scheme
the cancellation or surrender of an option under an employee scheme
transfers of securities by an independent trustee of an employee share scheme to a beneficiary who is not a person
bona fide gifts to a Director by a third party
transfers of securities in the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the entity) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the securities of the entity by that trust provided the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the restricted person

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: The Company may, at its discretion, make any clearance granted in accordance with this Clause 1.11 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the securities in the Company may be sold to satisfy a margin call).

external_documents: Continuous Disclosure Policy (Corporate Governance Charter, section 4)
exemption_authority: No exemption exists for the absolute hedging ban in 1.10. Exceptional-circumstances clearance under 1.4/1.8 is limited to permitting a sale (never a purchase) during a prohibited period, decided by the Chairperson (or another Director if the Chairperson is involved) in their sole discretion, and is unavailable if there is a matter about which there is inside information. Margin lending arrangements under 1.11 may be cleared by the Company's consent, conditional on terms the Company sees fit.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights). Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar's put and call legs are hedging arrangements under this definition and are banned outright for all Restricted Persons and associated parties, with no clearance route, no vesting-based carve-out and no stated exemption authority.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin loan consent and margin-call control
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent ... The Company may ... make any clearance granted ... conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the securities ... may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even absent the hedging ban, the loan leg secured on the collared shares would need the Company's prior consent, and the Company can condition that consent on when the bank may sell the shares on a margin call, constraining enforcement of the bank's security.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the hedging ban were lifted, the only prohibited-period clearance route permits a sale, not entry into a derivative or loan, so it offers no mechanism to establish the collar itself during a blackout.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's securities at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An undiscloseable Board embargo could block any residual dealing, unwind or refinancing step connected with the facility without notice.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no venue or vesting limitation on hedging
bespoke_clauses.clause: hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to unvested or plan securities, so it also forecloses hedging fully vested, unrestricted shareholdings, unlike policies that only restrict hedging of unvested equity.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 1.10 imposes an absolute, unqualified prohibition on Restricted Persons and their associated parties entering into any hedging arrangement, including financial products that limit the economic risk of holding Company securities, with no clearance mechanism, no vesting-based carve-out and no stated exemption authority, so the purchased put and written call legs cannot be entered at all. The loan leg would separately require the Company's prior consent under the margin lending clause (1.11), which may cover a bank-provided securities-backed facility given its broad wording, and the Company can condition that consent on the circumstances in which the shares may be sold to satisfy a call, giving it practical control over enforcement. The only prohibited-period clearance mechanism (1.4/1.8) permits a sale but never a purchase, so it cannot be used to establish the collar even in exceptional circumstances. The Board also retains an unfettered, potentially undisclosed discretion to embargo trading at any time. Absent a policy amendment or a bespoke Board waiver (neither of which is provided for), this policy forecloses the funded collar structure entirely.
